content.title: About
content.content: Spanish rice, no added fat is a cooked rice dish prepared in the traditional Spanish style with tomatoes, vegetables and spices, but without oil or other fats. It retains the bright flavor and aroma while keeping fat calories to a minimum.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Spanish rice (paella) is often cooked with olive oil, but the fat‑free version uses only water and vegetable broth.
Rice in Spain is mainly grown in the Valencia and Aragon regions, where the climate is ideal for high‑quality grains.
The dish is commonly served with seafood, but the fat‑free version relies solely on vegetables, making it suitable for vegetarians.
Tomatoes used in the recipe are rich in lycopene, enhancing the dish’s antioxidant profile.
The characteristic aroma is preserved by spices such as saffron, paprika and garlic, even without added fat.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes the dish suitable for low‑fat and reduced‑calorie diets.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides sustained energy release, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains thiamine, niacin and vitamin B6, which support metabolic processes.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and saffron add lycopene and crocin, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables aids gut function and promotes satiety.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: While rice itself is gluten‑free, the prepared product may be made in a kitchen where gluten is present, posing a risk for people with celiac disease.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice has a high GI, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Sodium in broth
items.content: Flavorful vegetable broth often contains added salt, which can increase sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a main dish or as a side to fish, chicken or legumes. It can be added to salads, packed in lunch boxes, or reheated in the microwave. Garnish with fresh herbs such as parsley or cilantro for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in freezer‑safe bags – they retain quality for up to 2 months. Reheat to at least 75 °C before consumption.
